architectures.description: One module per feature and per data source. Simple, and what most apps need.
architectures.title: Compact

architectures.description: Each feature and data module split into :api and :impl, for larger teams.
architectures.title: Modular

design_styles.description: Cool neutrals, hairline outlines, a floating tab bar. Tools, finance, admin.
design_styles.title: Utility

design_styles.description: Brand-tinted surfaces, pill buttons, heavier headlines, a floating tab bar. Feeds and chat.
design_styles.title: Social

design_styles.description: Warm paper and ink, large tight display type, underlined fields. Reading and news.
design_styles.title: Editorial

design_styles.description: Cream surfaces, extra-bold type, thick outlines and offset shadows. Games and kids.
design_styles.title: Playful

features.description: The server can require an update (HTTP 426, or a minimum-version header) or announce maintenance (503), and the app shows a full-screen message for either, whichever screen made the call.
features.headline: Turn away old versions, announce downtime
features.title: Forced update and maintenance screens

features.description: Remote images with a skeleton placeholder and a failure glyph.
features.headline: Load images from URLs
features.title: Image loading (Coil)

features.description: A Room 3 database with a table per domain, emptied when the person signs out. With the reference feature, its list is offline-first: what was fetched last is on screen at once, and a refresh writes the server's answer into the table.
features.headline: Keep the app's own data on the device
features.title: App database (Room 3)

features.description: One HTTP client for the whole app: typed results, the session's token read for every request and refreshed one call at a time, every failure classified (offline, timeout, the server's own error code, an unreadable body), and the connection state as a hint a screen can show.
features.headline: Talk to a REST API
features.title: REST networking (Ktor)

features.description: Changes made without a connection are queued and sent when one returns, by a WorkManager worker that waits for the network. Refusals are kept with the server's answer; rate limits and timeouts are retried. WorkManager carries a copy of Room of its own, so this adds more code than it looks.
features.headline: Send what was written offline
features.title: Offline request queue

features.description: A Feed tab on Paging 3: pages load as you scroll, a failed page keeps what is already loaded and offers a retry, and pull to refresh reloads from where you are. The list component lives in core/ui for your own feeds.
features.headline: An endless feed that loads as you scroll
features.title: Paged feed

features.description: One long-lived socket that is open while the app is in front: pings, a backoff that grows until a frame gets through, the new token after an account change, and a connection state a screen can render.
features.headline: Keep a live connection open
features.title: WebSocket

features.description: A fingerprint, face or screen-lock prompt over the app at launch and after half a minute away, a setting to turn it on, and the app kept out of the task switcher's thumbnail while it is on.
features.headline: Ask for a fingerprint on return
features.title: Biometric app lock

features.description: Three screens against your auth endpoints, writing the encrypted token store — with server-side field errors mapped back onto the inputs that caused them.
features.headline: Sign in, sign up, reset password
features.title: Sign in, sign up and password reset

features.description: A Continue with Google button on the sign-in screen through Credential Manager. The ID token goes to your backend, which answers with its own tokens like any sign-in.
features.headline: Continue with Google
features.title: Sign in with Google

features.description: A Profile tab with an avatar, name and bio, saved on the device per user. With the media picker on, the avatar can be a photo.
features.headline: A profile tab with a photo
features.title: Profile screen

features.description: Each field's text lives in a TextFieldState the ViewModel owns, so typing never waits on a state update and survives process death; validators return error codes the screen turns into copy, and server-side errors map back onto the fields that caused them.
features.headline: Validate forms properly
features.title: Form state and validation

features.description: A Language row in settings. Uses the system's per-app language on Android 13+ so it also appears in the phone's settings, and applies it by hand on older releases.
features.headline: Let people pick the app's language
features.title: In-app language picker

features.description: The real dependency list, generated from the resolved classpath at build time and rendered by the design system. The build also fails on a licence the project has not allowed.
features.headline: Show the licences you have to show
features.title: Open source licences screen

features.description: A paged walkthrough shown once, recorded in the preference store. Skipping counts as finishing, so it never comes back on the next launch.
features.headline: A first-run walkthrough
features.title: Onboarding flow

features.description: A working list + detail feature against a live public API, with its tests. Proves every wire on first run; delete it once your own first feature exists.
features.headline: A working screen to learn from
features.title: Reference feature

features.description: A Search tab: results as you type with a debounce, recent searches kept per user, and the empty, no-results and error states already drawn.
features.headline: Search as you type
features.title: Search screen

features.description: Theme switch, analytics opt-out, sign-out with confirmation and the build version — wired to the preference store and the session.
features.headline: A settings screen
features.title: Settings screen

features.description: Web pages open in a Custom Tab coloured like the app rather than in the browser. Adds privacy and terms links to settings when settings is on.
features.headline: Open web pages without leaving the app
features.title: In-app browser

features.description: A custom scheme plus verified App Links. Each feature maps its own links to a screen; a link is held until onboarding, sign-in and the startup checks are done, opens on the tab that owns the screen, and is never replayed from Recents or after rotation.
features.headline: Open the app from a link
features.title: Deep linking

features.description: The system photo picker and the camera app, with no permissions to ask for, and one image compressor that turns a picked photo upright, scales it and writes a copy the app owns.
features.headline: Pick, take and shrink photos
features.title: Photo picker, camera and compression

features.description: A newer build offered once per launch through Play's own sheet and never offered again once turned down, a restart only when the person asks for it, and a rating prompt on a schedule Play honours.
features.headline: Offer updates and ask for ratings
features.title: Play in-app update and review prompts

features.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging alone: notification channels, the permission asked for at the end of onboarding and offered again in settings, a tap that opens the app, a lock-screen-safe preview, and registration that is renewed only when it changes and removed at sign-out.
features.headline: Receive push notifications
features.title: Push notifications (FCM)

features.description: AnalyticsTracker and CrashReporter interfaces that write nothing until a vendor is bound, the settings opt-out applied to both, logged errors kept as breadcrumbs, and janky frames counted on the device.
features.headline: Track events and crashes, vendor-free
features.title: Analytics and crash-reporting seam

features.description: Crashlytics behind the crash-reporting seam: crashes and unhandled errors are reported, every logged error is a breadcrumb, and the R8 mapping is uploaded only by a release build that asks for it.
features.headline: Send crashes to Firebase
features.title: Firebase Crashlytics

features.description: A badge docked to the screen's edge in dev and debug builds, which can be dragged out of the way, and a panel behind it with the last 200 requests (credentials redacted), their timing and failure rate, and the build's details. Absent from a production build rather than hidden in one.
features.headline: See every request the app made
features.title: On-device inspector

features.description: The google-services plugin and the project file it reads. Arrives with push, Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics or Remote Config, each of which adds only its own SDK.
features.headline: The Firebase project file
features.title: Firebase

features.description: Firebase Analytics behind the analytics seam, switched off when the person opts out in settings. It brings the advertising-id permissions with it, which is why it is a choice of its own.
features.headline: Send analytics to Firebase
features.title: Firebase Analytics

features.description: Typed flags declared in one file with their defaults beside them, read or observed through an interface that resolves locally until a vendor is bound, and overridable by hand in the inspector.
features.headline: Turn a feature on without shipping
features.title: Feature flag seam

features.description: Frames per second at the display's real rate and the janky-frame share under the DEV badge, and a Performance tab in the inspector: frame times against the 60, 90 and 120 Hz budgets, frames per second over time, a main-thread time histogram, jank by screen, memory over time, start-up and request timings, and an optimisation score from 0 to 100 with a fix for every lost point. A structured logcat summary and an exported JSON and Markdown report. On in debug builds, a switch away in dev release builds, and absent from production builds; while it is off it puts nothing on the window. It lives in the on-device inspector, so it is on by default wherever the inspector is chosen, as in the Standard preset.
features.headline: FPS, jank, graphs and a score beside the DEV badge
features.title: Live performance overlay

features.description: Feature flags read from Remote Config: fetched at start-up, updated while the app is open when the console publishes a change, and fetched on every start in a debug build.
features.headline: Change feature flags from the console
features.title: Firebase Remote Config

features.description: A second installable app showing every component and token, in the project's own design and motion style. A bar switches theme, style, motion, right-to-left, font scale and reduced motion live; each page opens directly with `--es section <Name>`, and a frame-time readout shows what each interaction costs. Depends on the design system alone, so design work rebuilds two modules.
features.headline: A second app showing every component
features.title: Component catalog app

features.description: A paging carousel that peeks at its neighbours, a list whose rows lift and reorder under the finger or with accessibility actions, and a full-screen image viewer with pinch zoom and swipe to dismiss.
features.headline: Carousels, drag to reorder, zoomable images
features.title: Carousel, reorderable list and image viewer

features.description: Stat tiles with a trend, a sparkline and a bar chart drawn in one pass each, key-value grids, a timeline, a data table with sticky totals and measured column widths, an animated counter and a star rating.
features.headline: Show numbers, charts and tables
features.title: Data display

features.description: A one-time-code field, decimal and money fields that keep the caret where the user typed, a phone field with a dial code, a stepper, a tag field, a select field, a range slider and a step indicator for multi-page forms.
features.headline: Fields for codes, money and more
features.title: Specialised form fields

features.description: The typefaces the spec names (DM Sans and JetBrains Mono unless you choose others), downloaded through the Play Services font provider in exactly the weights the design style draws with. They are fetched while the splash is up; a launch where they take longer than 150 ms draws in the platform font throughout, so text never swaps under the reader.
features.headline: Use any Google Font
features.title: Downloadable Google Font

features.description: The foundation liquid glass is drawn with, on Kyant's backdrop library: the glass tier the device can afford (live, live without the lens, frosted, solid), which battery saver, heat, a GPU that falls behind and Reduce transparency step down; the scene backdrop floating chrome samples; glass surfaces; and the travelling lens. No bar, sheet or other component draws with it yet: the project gets the pieces and Kyant's two libraries, and its look does not change.
features.headline: Glass tiers, a backdrop and a lens to build glass chrome on; nothing uses them yet
features.title: Liquid glass foundation

features.description: An inline month calendar with limits and disabled days, iOS-style wheel pickers for any list, a time picker built from wheels, and compact date and time pills that open them in a sheet.
features.headline: Pick dates and times inline
features.title: Date and time pickers

features.description: A GitHub Actions workflow that runs `check` (unit tests, lint, the code rules, the module graph and the Compose stability gate) and assembles the debug and release builds on every push and pull request, uploading the reports when something fails.
features.headline: Build and test every push on GitHub
features.title: Continuous integration

features.description: One merged coverage number for the whole project with a floor the build enforces, generated code excluded so the report is about code somebody wrote.
features.headline: Fail a build that drops coverage
features.title: Coverage floor (Kover)

features.description: Names every module declaring a dependency it never uses, or using one it only gets transitively — the second being the failure that surfaces months later as an unrelated module breaking. `./gradlew buildHealth` writes the report; it is advice rather than a gate, because two of this template's own decisions produce advice it is right to ignore.
features.headline: See which dependencies nobody uses
features.title: Dependency health report

features.description: Spotless runs ktlint's Android Studio style over every Kotlin and Gradle file: `check` fails on a file that is not formatted and `spotlessApply` fixes it. The rules live in .editorconfig, which Android Studio reads too.
features.headline: One code style, checked on every build
features.title: Formatting (Spotless + ktlint)

features.description: Memory-leak detection in debug builds.
features.headline: Find memory leaks in debug builds
features.title: LeakCanary (debug only)

features.description: A macrobenchmark module (cold and warm start, tab switch, push and pop, predictive back, rapid Back, scroll) that runs against the dev flavour, the baseline profile generator, tools/perf (one command that installs a release build, measures every journey on a connected phone and fails on the frame-time gates) and tools/adaptive (the app across window sizes, folds, a second window and the keyboard on an emulator). Every project ships the checked-in baseline profiles without it.
features.headline: Measure smoothness on a real phone
features.title: Performance harness

options.description: Every non-UI part of the project: the modules, MVI, Navigation 3 with deep links and process-death restore, data, DI, tests and every build guard. core:designsystem is a theme skeleton (AppTheme with colour, type, spacing, shape and motion slots, filled with neutral values and your colours and font) with no components; each screen is a one-line placeholder route over its ViewModel, and the app opens on a blank start screen. The developer panel, the performance overlay and LeakCanary stay.

disables.reason: The catalog app shows the design system's components, and this project has none.
Carousels, reorderable lists and the image viewer are components; build yours on the theme skeleton.
Stat tiles, charts and tables are components; build yours on the theme skeleton.
Code, money and phone fields are components; form state and validation (forms) stay.
Calendars and wheel pickers are components; build yours on the theme skeleton.
Glass is drawn by components and the shell, which this project leaves to your design system.

feature_copy.description: The server can require an update (HTTP 426, or a minimum-version header) or announce maintenance (503), whichever screen made the call, and the app covers itself with a placeholder for either: a tap opens the store listing for an update and retries during maintenance, until your own design replaces the placeholder.
feature_copy.headline: Turn away old versions, announce downtime

feature_copy.description: Coil's image loader on the app's own HTTP client, sharing its connections and its certificate pins, ready for the image component your design system draws.
feature_copy.headline: Load images from URLs

feature_copy.description: A Room 3 database with a table per domain, emptied when the person signs out. With the reference feature, its list is offline-first: the list's state holds what was fetched last at once, and a refresh writes the server's answer into the table.
feature_copy.headline: Keep the app's own data on the device

feature_copy.description: The feed's data on Paging 3, behind its ViewModel and a placeholder route: pages load as the list asks for them, a failed page keeps what is already loaded and can be retried, and a refresh reloads from where the reader is. The list it pages into is yours to build.
feature_copy.headline: Paged loading for an endless feed

feature_copy.description: A fingerprint, face or screen-lock prompt at launch and after half a minute away, over a placeholder cover that asks again on a tap, and the app kept out of the task switcher's thumbnail while the lock is on. It starts off: the settings ViewModel's AppLockToggled turns it on, from the switch your settings screen draws.
feature_copy.headline: Ask for a fingerprint on return

feature_copy.description: Sign-in, sign-up and password-reset ViewModels against your auth endpoints, behind three placeholder routes, writing the encrypted token store. Their form state holds each field's text and error, with the server's field errors mapped back onto the field that caused them, for the inputs your sign-in screen draws.
feature_copy.headline: Sign in, sign up, reset password

feature_copy.description: Credential Manager's Google sign-in, ready for the control your sign-in screen draws to hand its ID token to the sign-in ViewModel. The token goes to your backend, which answers with its own tokens like any sign-in.
feature_copy.headline: Sign in with a Google account

feature_copy.description: A name, a bio and an avatar, saved on the device per user, behind the profile's ViewModel and a placeholder route. With the media picker on, the ViewModel takes a picked photo for the avatar.
feature_copy.headline: A profile with a photo, per user

feature_copy.description: AppLocales sets and reads the app's own language: the system's per-app language on Android 13+, so the choice also appears in the phone's settings, applied by hand on older releases. The settings ViewModel holds it in its state and applies a choice through its route, for the picker your settings screen draws.
feature_copy.headline: Let people pick the app's language

feature_copy.description: The real dependency list, generated from the resolved classpath at build time and loaded by its ViewModel behind a placeholder route. The build also fails on a licence the project has not allowed.
feature_copy.headline: Show the licences you have to show

feature_copy.description: An onboarding ViewModel over three pages of copy in resources, behind a placeholder route: finishing and skipping both record it in the preference store, so a person goes through it once. A first launch still opens on the blank start screen; AppRoot can open onboarding instead once you draw its pages.
feature_copy.headline: Record a first run once

feature_copy.description: A list + detail feature against a live public API, with its tests: keys, ViewModels, repository and navigation behind two placeholder routes that load and open items as the finished ones will. Copy its shape for your first feature, then delete it.
feature_copy.headline: A worked feature to learn from

feature_copy.description: Results as you type with a debounce, and recent searches kept per user, behind the search ViewModel and a placeholder route; its state holds the results, whether they are loading and why they failed.
feature_copy.headline: Search as you type

feature_copy.description: The settings ViewModel, wired to the preference store and the session: theme, analytics opt-out, haptics and sign-out, with the build version in its state, behind a placeholder route. Your settings screen draws the switches and asks before it sends sign-out.
feature_copy.headline: Settings state over the preference store

feature_copy.description: Web pages open in a Custom Tab coloured like the app rather than in the browser, through rememberInAppBrowser() in core:ui, for the links you draw. With settings on, the settings module's resources hold the privacy and terms addresses for the links your settings screen draws.
feature_copy.headline: Open web pages without leaving the app

feature_copy.description: A custom scheme plus verified App Links. Each feature maps its own links to a destination; a link is held until start-up has read the settings and the session, then opens on the back stack, which survives process death, over the start screen, whether or not anyone is signed in: the project has no entry gates until you add yours. A link is never replayed from Recents or after rotation.
feature_copy.headline: Open the app from a link

feature_copy.description: rememberMediaPicker() for the screen that asks: the system photo picker and the camera app, with no permissions to ask for, and one image compressor that turns a picked photo upright, scales it and writes a copy the app owns.
feature_copy.headline: Pick, take and shrink photos

feature_copy.description: A newer build offered once per launch through Play's own sheet and never offered again once turned down, and a rating prompt on a schedule Play honours. A downloaded update installs when the app next goes to the background; the offer to restart into it at once goes to LocalMessagePresenter, which logs it until your design system shows messages.
feature_copy.headline: Offer updates and ask for ratings

feature_copy.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging alone: notification channels, a tap that opens the app, a lock-screen-safe preview, and registration that is renewed only when it changes and removed at sign-out. Nothing asks for the notification permission yet: rememberNotificationPermission() is ready for the screen you build to ask from, and on Android 13 and up notifications stay off until it does.
feature_copy.headline: Receive push notifications

feature_copy.description: Firebase Analytics behind the analytics seam, switched off by the analytics opt-out in the preference store; the switch that sets it is your settings screen's to draw. It brings the advertising-id permissions with it, which is why it is a choice of its own.
feature_copy.headline: Send analytics to Firebase

feature_copy.description: A macrobenchmark module for cold and warm start to the start screen, with and without the baseline profile, run against the dev flavour, and the baseline profile generator that records the profile every build ships. The journey benchmarks and the frame-time scripts come with the components they measure.
feature_copy.headline: Measure start-up on a real phone

options.headline: Setup only: the architecture, every build guard and a theme skeleton, without UI components

hides.reason: Your design system decides corners, surfaces and type voice; the theme starts from neutral values.
Your components decide their motion; the theme keeps neutral springs and reduce-motion.

options.module_copy: Each gets a :data module with its repository and a :feature module with list and detail ViewModels behind placeholder routes, their keys and navigation wiring, and a ViewModel test.

preset_copy.description: The architecture, a theme skeleton and every build guard, with networking, image loading, your font, leak detection in debug builds, deep links and CI. The app opens on a blank start screen for your design system to build on.

The lean set plus the logic of sign-in, onboarding, settings and the app's own language, each behind a placeholder route, with the in-app browser, feature flags, the developer panel with its performance overlay, a local database and the reference list-detail feature to copy. What most products want on day one, ready for your own design system.
Every feature that does not need UI components, working together: the template's own proof that they coexist without them. Delete what you do not need.
